findings.reason: without the grammar constraint §3 either blocks silently on transfer names or attempts a grammar change the plan never scopes, which is the one outcome the evidence already rules out.
findings.text: rule 6 states that "A transfer between two populations names both donor and recipient" while the cited evidence (`incumbent-failures-under-codified-rules.json`, `rules.transfer`) reads "…names both donor and recipient; the grammar has no form for this today"; the limitation is dropped, so §3's "Each name §2 flags is repaired once, changing only what its rule names" sends a worker at repairs the grammar cannot express, with no route for them

findings.reason: the collision case is the highest-consequence repair path (evidence records 4 of 9 frontier blocks as `collision`), and an unresolved contradiction there decides which name survives the catalog.
findings.text: §3 says "A repair whose new name collides with an existing name is not applied. It is listed as a duplicate, with the name to keep, for the lead to rule on", but rule 7 at line 42 says "A repair that collides with an existing name marks a duplicate to retire" — the two dispositions of the same case are opposite (withhold the repair versus apply it and retire the duplicate), so a worker resolves the rule it was handed arbitrarily

findings.reason: the set §3 repairs is what a worker reads off the page, and the mismatch sends a rename at names the plan says no one may decide yet.
findings.text: §3 scopes its work as "Each name §2 flags", but §2 (line 59–64) defines three results, one of which is "an edge case the rules do not settle"; the plan's own text says edge cases are put to the lead (line 68), so "each name §2 flags" would repair the very names waiting on a ruling, while §3's acceptance measure silently counts only "sampled names that break a rule"

findings.reason: the reading's recorded version is the only provenance a later repair depends on, and a version that can move mid-read makes that provenance unfalsifiable.
findings.text: §2 pins the reading to "the rules file at a recorded version" and also requires that "Each ruling the lead gives is added to the rules file's log" (line 68), so the file's version moves while the catalog is being read; the plan states no epoch rule, leaving a worker unable to say whether a name read before a ruling was read under the version it records
